raw: Act 3, Scene 2 — A Room in Capulet’s House

sentences.en: A Room in Capulet’s House
sentences.ko: 캐퓰릿 집의 방

summary.en: Juliet waits for her wedding night. The Nurse brings the news that Romeo has killed Tybalt and must leave the city.
summary.ko: 줄리엣은 첫날밤을 기다린다. 유모가 로미오가 티볼트를 죽이고 도시를 떠나야 한다는 소식을 전한다.

raw: Enter Juliet.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Gallop apace, you fiery-footed steeds,
Towards Phoebus’ lodging. Such a waggoner
As Phaeton would whip you to the west
And bring in cloudy night immediately.
Spread thy close curtain, love-performing night,
That runaway’s eyes may wink, and Romeo
Leap to these arms, untalk’d of and unseen.
Lovers can see to do their amorous rites
By their own beauties: or, if love be blind,
It best agrees with night. Come, civil night,
Thou sober-suited matron, all in black,
And learn me how to lose a winning match,
Play’d for a pair of stainless maidenhoods.
Hood my unmann’d blood, bating in my cheeks,
With thy black mantle, till strange love, grow bold,
Think true love acted simple modesty.
Come, night, come Romeo; come, thou day in night;
For thou wilt lie upon the wings of night
Whiter than new snow upon a raven’s back.
Come gentle night, come loving black-brow’d night,
Give me my Romeo, and when I shall die,
Take him and cut him out in little stars,
And he will make the face of heaven so fine
That all the world will be in love with night,
And pay no worship to the garish sun.
O, I have bought the mansion of a love,
But not possess’d it; and though I am sold,
Not yet enjoy’d. So tedious is this day
As is the night before some festival
To an impatient child that hath new robes
And may not wear them. O, here comes my Nurse,
And she brings news, and every tongue that speaks
But Romeo’s name speaks heavenly eloquence.

sentences.en: I wish this day would end!
sentences.ko: 이 날이 빨리 끝났으면 좋겠다!

sentences.en: Gallop fast, you fiery horses of the sun, and pull it west.
sentences.ko: 태양의 불타는 말들아, 서쪽으로 달려가라.

sentences.en: A driver like Phaeton would whip you west and bring in a cloudy night immediately.
sentences.ko: 파에톤 같은 마부라면 너희를 서쪽으로 채찍질해 당장 어두운 밤을 데려올 텐데.

sentences.en: Spread your close curtain, love-performing night, so that prying eyes may close.
sentences.ko: 사랑을 행하는 밤아, 네 검은 커튼을 펼쳐서 방해하는 시선을 막아다오.

sentences.en: Then Romeo can leap into my arms, unseen and untalked of.
sentences.ko: 그러면 로미오가 아무도 모르게 내 품으로 뛰어들 수 있을 것이다.

sentences.en: Lovers can see to perform their romantic acts by their own beauty.
sentences.ko: 연인들은 서로의 아름다움만으로도 사랑을 나눌 수 있다.

sentences.en: Or if love is blind, it fits best with the night.
sentences.ko: 혹은 사랑이 눈이 멀었다면, 밤과 가장 잘 어울린다.

sentences.en: Come, serious night; you are like a serious older woman, all in black.
sentences.ko: 점잖은 밤아 오라, 온통 검은 옷을 입은 근엄한 부인 같은 밤아.

sentences.en: Teach me how to lose a game that I win by losing.
sentences.ko: 잃어야 이기는 이 놀이에서 지는 법을 가르쳐 다오.

sentences.en: In it, two virgins give themselves to each other.
sentences.ko: 그 안에서 두 처녀가 서로에게 자신을 내어준다.

sentences.en: Hide the shy blood rushing to my cheeks with your black cloak until my shy love grows bold.
sentences.ko: 내 수줍은 사랑이 용기를 얻을 때까지, 너의 검은 망토로 내 뺨에 달아오르는 피를 숨겨다오.

sentences.en: Then it will see that true love is pure.
sentences.ko: 그러면 진정한 사랑이 순수하다는 것을 알게 될 것이다.

sentences.en: Come, night, come Romeo; come, you day in the night.
sentences.ko: 밤아 오라, 로미오야 오라. 밤속의 낮이여, 오라.

sentences.en: You will lie on the wings of night and be whiter than new snow on a raven's back.
sentences.ko: 너는 밤의 날개 위에 누워, 까마귀 등에 내린 새 눈보다 하얗게 빛나리라.

sentences.en: Come gentle night, come loving black-brow'd night, and give me my Romeo.
sentences.ko: 부드러운 밤아, 사랑스러운 검은 눈썹의 밤아, 나의 로미오를 데려다오.

sentences.en: And when I die, take him and cut him into little stars.
sentences.ko: 그리고 내가 죽으면 그를 데려가 작은 별들로 쪼개어 다오.

sentences.en: He will make the face of heaven so fine.
sentences.ko: 그는 하늘의 얼굴을 아주 아름답게 만들 것이다.

sentences.en: All the world will be in love with the night.
sentences.ko: 온 세상이 밤과 사랑에 빠질 것이다.

sentences.en: No one will worship the bright sun.
sentences.ko: 아무도 밝은 태양을 숭배하지 않을 것이다.

sentences.en: Oh, I have bought the house of a love, but I do not possess it yet.
sentences.ko: 오, 나는 사랑의 집을 샀지만 아직 들어가 살지 못했다.

sentences.en: And though I have been sold to him, he has not yet enjoyed me.
sentences.ko: 나는 그에게 팔렸지만 그는 아직 나를 누리지 못했다.

sentences.en: This day is as tedious as the night before a festival to an impatient child with new clothes.
sentences.ko: 오늘은 새 옷을 받고도 입지 못하는 아이의 축제 전날 밤처럼 지루하다.

sentences.en: The child cannot wear them yet.
sentences.ko: 그 아이는 아직 새 옷을 입을 수 없다.

sentences.en: Look, here comes my Nurse, and she brings news.
sentences.ko: 보라, 유모가 소식을 가지고 온다.

sentences.en: Anyone who even says Romeo's name sounds like heaven to me.
sentences.ko: 누구든 로미오의 이름을 말하기만 해도 나에게는 천국처럼 들린다.

raw: Enter Nurse, with cords.

sentences.ko: 유모가 밧줄을 들고 들어온다.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Now, Nurse, what news? What hast thou there?
The cords that Romeo bid thee fetch?

sentences.en: Now, Nurse, what news?
sentences.ko: 자, 유모, 무슨 소식이야?

sentences.en: What do you have there?
sentences.ko: 거기 든 게 뭐야?

sentences.en: Are these the ropes that Romeo told you to fetch?
sentences.ko: 로미오가 가져오라고 한 그 밧줄이야?

speaker: NURSE
raw: Ay, ay, the cords.

sentences.en: Yes, yes, the ropes.
sentences.ko: 그래, 그래, 밧줄이야.

raw: Throws them down.

sentences.en: The Nurse throws them down.
sentences.ko: 유모가 그것들을 내던진다.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Ay me, what news? Why dost thou wring thy hands?

sentences.en: Oh me, what news?
sentences.ko: 아이고, 무슨 소식이야?

sentences.en: Why do you wring your hands?
sentences.ko: 왜 손을 쥐어짜?

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Ah, well-a-day, he’s dead, he’s dead, he’s dead!
We are undone, lady, we are undone.
Alack the day, he’s gone, he’s kill’d, he’s dead.

sentences.en: Oh, no, he is dead.
sentences.ko: 아이고, 그가 죽었어.

sentences.en: He is dead, he is dead!
sentences.ko: 죽었어, 죽었다고!

sentences.en: We are ruined, lady, we are ruined.
sentences.ko: 우린 끝났어, 아가씨, 모든 게 끝났어.

sentences.en: Alas, the day, he is gone.
sentences.ko: 아이고 이 날, 가 버렸어.

sentences.en: He is killed, he is dead.
sentences.ko: 살해당했어, 죽었다고.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Can heaven be so envious?

sentences.en: Can heaven be so cruel?
sentences.ko: 하늘이 이토록 잔인할 수 있니?

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Romeo can,
Though heaven cannot. O Romeo, Romeo.
Who ever would have thought it? Romeo!

sentences.en: Romeo can, even though heaven cannot.
sentences.ko: 하늘은 못 해도 로미오는 할 수 있지.

sentences.en: Oh Romeo, Romeo, who ever would have thought it? Romeo!
sentences.ko: 오 로미오, 로미오, 누가 이런 일을 상상이나 했겠어? 로미오!

speaker: JULIET
raw:
What devil art thou, that dost torment me thus?
This torture should be roar’d in dismal hell.
Hath Romeo slain himself? Say thou but Ay,
And that bare vowel I shall poison more
Than the death-darting eye of cockatrice.
I am not I if there be such an I;
Or those eyes shut that make thee answer Ay.
If he be slain, say Ay; or if not, No.
Brief sounds determine of my weal or woe.

sentences.en: What devil are you that you torment me like this?
sentences.ko: 너는 무슨 악마길래 나를 이렇게 괴롭혀?

sentences.en: This torture should be shouted in dark hell.
sentences.ko: 이런 고문은 어두운 지옥에서나 울부짖을 일이야.

sentences.en: Has Romeo killed himself?
sentences.ko: 로미오가 자살한 거니?

sentences.en: Say only 'Yes' to me.
sentences.ko: '응'이라고만 해 봐.

sentences.en: That one little 'yes' will poison me more than a monster that kills with one look.
sentences.ko: 그 짧은 '응' 한마디가 눈빛만으로 사람을 죽이는 괴물보다 더 지독한 독이 될 거야.

sentences.en: If you say 'yes', I am no longer myself.
sentences.ko: 네가 '응'이라고 하면, 난 더 이상 내가 아니게 돼.

sentences.en: If his eyes are closed forever, say 'yes'.
sentences.ko: 그의 눈이 영원히 감겼다면, '응'이라고 해.

sentences.en: If he is killed, say 'Yes'.
sentences.ko: 그가 죽었다면, '응'이라고 해.

sentences.en: If he is not, say 'No'.
sentences.ko: 아니라면, '아니'라고 해.

sentences.en: Short sounds decide my happiness or my sadness.
sentences.ko: 짧은 대답 하나에 나의 행복과 슬픔이 결정돼.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
I saw the wound, I saw it with mine eyes,
God save the mark!—here on his manly breast.
A piteous corse, a bloody piteous corse;
Pale, pale as ashes, all bedaub’d in blood,
All in gore-blood. I swounded at the sight.

sentences.en: I saw the wound and I saw it with my own eyes.
sentences.ko: 상처를 봤어, 내 눈으로 직접 봤다고.

sentences.en: God forgive me for saying it!
sentences.ko: 하나님 맙소사!

sentences.en: It was here on his manly chest.
sentences.ko: 그의 늠름한 가슴 위에 있었어.

sentences.en: A pitiful body, a bloody and pitiful body.
sentences.ko: 가련한 몸, 피투성이가 된 가련한 몸.

sentences.en: He was pale as ashes and covered in blood.
sentences.ko: 그는 재처럼 창백했고 온몸이 피로 뒤덮였어.

sentences.en: He was all in gore-blood.
sentences.ko: 온통 엉긴 피투성이였어.

sentences.en: I fainted at the sight.
sentences.ko: 그 모습을 보고 난 기절했어.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
O, break, my heart. Poor bankrout, break at once.
To prison, eyes; ne’er look on liberty.
Vile earth to earth resign; end motion here,
And thou and Romeo press one heavy bier.

sentences.en: Oh, break my heart.
sentences.ko: 오, 내 심장아, 부서져라.

sentences.en: My poor heart, you have lost everything, so break now.
sentences.ko: 가여운 내 심장아, 모든 걸 잃었으니 이제 부서져라.

sentences.en: To prison, eyes; never look on liberty.
sentences.ko: 눈아, 감옥에 들어가라. 다시는 자유를 보지 마라.

sentences.en: My body, go back to the earth.
sentences.ko: 내 몸아, 다시 흙으로 돌아가라.

sentences.en: Stop moving now.
sentences.ko: 이제 움직임을 멈춰라.

sentences.en: Lie with Romeo in one coffin.
sentences.ko: 로미오와 한 관 속에 누워라.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
O Tybalt, Tybalt, the best friend I had.
O courteous Tybalt, honest gentleman!
That ever I should live to see thee dead.

sentences.en: Oh Tybalt, Tybalt, the best friend I had.
sentences.ko: 아이고 티볼트, 티볼트, 내 제일 좋은 친구.

sentences.en: Oh courteous Tybalt, honest gentleman!
sentences.ko: 친절하고 정직한 신사였던 티볼트!

sentences.en: That I should live to see you dead.
sentences.ko: 살다 살다 네가 죽은 걸 보게 되다니.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
What storm is this that blows so contrary?
Is Romeo slaughter’d and is Tybalt dead?
My dearest cousin, and my dearer lord?
Then dreadful trumpet sound the general doom,
For who is living, if those two are gone?

sentences.en: What storm is this that blows from both directions?
sentences.ko: 양쪽에서 몰아치는 이 폭풍은 대체 뭐지?

sentences.en: Is Romeo killed and is Tybalt dead?
sentences.ko: 로미오가 죽고 티볼트도 죽은 건가?

sentences.en: My dearest cousin and my dearer lord?
sentences.ko: 가장 소중한 사촌과 더 소중한 내 남편이?

sentences.en: Then let the terrible trumpet sound the final doom.
sentences.ko: 그렇다면 무서운 나팔아, 세상의 종말을 울려라.

sentences.en: For who is living if those two are gone?
sentences.ko: 그 두 사람이 없다면 누가 살아 있다 하겠어?

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Tybalt is gone, and Romeo banished,
Romeo that kill’d him, he is banished.

sentences.en: Tybalt is gone, and Romeo is banished, sent away from the city forever.
sentences.ko: 티볼트는 죽고, 로미오는 추방당했어. 이 도시에서 영원히 쫓겨난 거야.

sentences.en: Romeo killed him, and he is banished.
sentences.ko: 티볼트를 죽인 로미오가 추방당했어.

speaker: JULIET
raw: O God! Did Romeo’s hand shed Tybalt’s blood?

sentences.en: Oh God!
sentences.ko: 오, 신이시여!

sentences.en: Did Romeo's hand shed Tybalt's blood?
sentences.ko: 로미오의 손이 티볼트의 피를 흘리게 했단 말이야?

speaker: NURSE
raw: It did, it did; alas the day, it did.

sentences.en: It did, it did, and what a terrible day!
sentences.ko: 그랬어, 그랬어. 정말 끔찍한 날이야!

sentences.en: It did.
sentences.ko: 그랬어.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
O serpent heart, hid with a flowering face!
Did ever dragon keep so fair a cave?
Beautiful tyrant, fiend angelical,
Dove-feather’d raven, wolvish-ravening lamb!
Despised substance of divinest show!
Just opposite to what thou justly seem’st,
A damned saint, an honourable villain!
O nature, what hadst thou to do in hell
When thou didst bower the spirit of a fiend
In mortal paradise of such sweet flesh?
Was ever book containing such vile matter
So fairly bound? O, that deceit should dwell
In such a gorgeous palace.

sentences.en: Oh, you have a snake's heart hidden by a beautiful face!
sentences.ko: 오, 아름다운 얼굴 뒤에 뱀의 심장을 숨기고 있구나!

sentences.en: Did a dragon ever keep such a beautiful cave?
sentences.ko: 용이 이렇게 아름다운 동굴에 숨어 산 적이 있었던가?

sentences.en: You are a beautiful tyrant and an angelic fiend.
sentences.ko: 너는 아름다운 폭군이자 천사 같은 악마야.

sentences.en: You are a dove-feathered raven and a wolf-like lamb!
sentences.ko: 너는 비둘기 깃털을 가진 까마귀이자 늑대 같은 어린 양이야!

sentences.en: You are a hated thing hidden in a divine show!
sentences.ko: 너는 신성한 모습 속에 숨겨진 증오스러운 존재야!

sentences.en: You are the opposite of what you seem to be.
sentences.ko: 너는 겉모습과는 정반대의 존재구나.

sentences.en: You are a damned saint and an honorable villain!
sentences.ko: 너는 저주받은 성자이자 명예로운 악당이야!

sentences.en: Oh, nature, why did you put the spirit of a demon in this mortal paradise of such sweet flesh?
sentences.ko: 오, 대자연이여, 왜 이 달콤한 살결의 지상 낙원에 악마의 영혼을 집어넣었나?

sentences.en: Was there ever a book with such bad content bound so beautifully?
sentences.ko: 이렇게 아름답게 제본된 책에 이런 나쁜 내용이 담긴 적이 있었나?

sentences.en: Oh, that such a lie should live in such a beautiful palace.
sentences.ko: 오, 이렇게 아름다운 궁전에 그런 거짓말이 살고 있다니.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
There’s no trust,
No faith, no honesty in men. All perjur’d,
All forsworn, all naught, all dissemblers.
Ah, where’s my man? Give me some aqua vitae.
These griefs, these woes, these sorrows make me old.
Shame come to Romeo.

sentences.en: There is no trust.
sentences.ko: 믿을 게 없어.

sentences.en: There is no faith or honesty in men.
sentences.ko: 남자들에게 믿음이나 정직 같은 건 없단다.

sentences.en: All are liars and all have broken their promises.
sentences.ko: 모두 거짓말쟁이고 맹세를 어기는 놈들이야.

sentences.en: All are worthless and all are pretending to be something they are not.
sentences.ko: 모두 쓸모없고 겉과 속이 달라.

sentences.en: Where is my man?
sentences.ko: 내 하인은 어디 있지?

sentences.en: Give me some strong alcohol.
sentences.ko: 독한 술 좀 줘.

sentences.en: These problems and sorrows make me old.
sentences.ko: 이런 문제와 슬픔 때문에 내가 늙는구나.

sentences.en: Shame on Romeo.
sentences.ko: 로미오는 창피한 줄 알아야 해.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Blister’d be thy tongue
For such a wish! He was not born to shame.
Upon his brow shame is asham’d to sit;
For ’tis a throne where honour may be crown’d
Sole monarch of the universal earth.
O, what a beast was I to chide at him!

sentences.en: May your tongue be blistered for such a wish!
sentences.ko: 그런 말을 하다니 네 혀에 물집이나 생겨라!

sentences.en: He was not born for shame.
sentences.ko: 그이는 수치를 당하려고 태어난 사람이 아니야.

sentences.en: Shame would be ashamed to sit on his forehead.
sentences.ko: 수치도 그이의 이마에 앉기를 부끄러워할걸.

sentences.en: It is a throne where honor can be crowned as the only ruler of the whole world.
sentences.ko: 그 이마는 명예가 온 세상의 유일한 왕으로 즉위할 왕좌야.

sentences.en: Oh, what a beast was I to scold him!
sentences.ko: 아, 그이를 욕하다니 난 얼마나 짐승 같았나!

speaker: NURSE
raw: Will you speak well of him that kill’d your cousin?

sentences.en: Will you speak well of the man who killed your cousin?
sentences.ko: 네 사촌을 죽인 남자를 좋게 말해줄 거니?

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Shall I speak ill of him that is my husband?
Ah, poor my lord, what tongue shall smooth thy name,
When I thy three-hours’ wife have mangled it?
But wherefore, villain, didst thou kill my cousin?
That villain cousin would have kill’d my husband.
Back, foolish tears, back to your native spring,
Your tributary drops belong to woe,
Which you mistaking offer up to joy.
My husband lives, that Tybalt would have slain,
And Tybalt’s dead, that would have slain my husband.
All this is comfort; wherefore weep I then?
Some word there was, worser than Tybalt’s death,
That murder’d me. I would forget it fain,
But O, it presses to my memory
Like damned guilty deeds to sinners’ minds.
Tybalt is dead, and Romeo banished.
That ‘banished,’ that one word ‘banished,’
Hath slain ten thousand Tybalts. Tybalt’s death
Was woe enough, if it had ended there.
Or if sour woe delights in fellowship,
And needly will be rank’d with other griefs,
Why follow’d not, when she said Tybalt’s dead,
Thy father or thy mother, nay or both,
Which modern lamentation might have mov’d?
But with a rear-ward following Tybalt’s death,
‘Romeo is banished’—to speak that word
Is father, mother, Tybalt, Romeo, Juliet,
All slain, all dead. Romeo is banished,
There is no end, no limit, measure, bound,
In that word’s death, no words can that woe sound.
Where is my father and my mother, Nurse?

sentences.en: Should I speak badly of him who is my husband?
sentences.ko: 내 남편인 사람을 나쁘게 말해야 해?

sentences.en: Oh, my poor husband!
sentences.ko: 오, 가여운 내 남편!

sentences.en: Who will say good things about you now?
sentences.ko: 이제 누가 그대 이름을 좋게 말해 줄까?

sentences.en: I, your wife of three hours, have attacked your name!
sentences.ko: 결혼한 지 세 시간 된 아내인 내가 그대 이름을 헐뜯었는데!

sentences.en: But why, villain, did you kill my cousin?
sentences.ko: 하지만 그대는 왜 내 사촌을 죽였어?

sentences.en: That villain cousin would have killed my husband.
sentences.ko: 그 악당 사촌이 내 남편을 죽이려 했으니까.

sentences.en: Go away, foolish tears, and go back to your source.
sentences.ko: 어리석은 눈물아, 물러가서 원래 있던 곳으로 돌아가라.

sentences.en: Your drops belong to sadness, but you offer them to joy by mistake.
sentences.ko: 네 눈물방울은 슬픔의 것이지만, 실수로 기쁨에 바쳐지고 있구나.

sentences.en: My husband, whom Tybalt wanted to kill, is alive.
sentences.ko: 티볼트가 죽이려 했던 내 남편은 살아있어.

sentences.en: And Tybalt, who wanted to kill my husband, is dead.
sentences.ko: 그리고 내 남편을 죽이려 했던 티볼트는 죽었어.

sentences.en: All of this is comfort, so why do I cry then?
sentences.ko: 이 모든 게 위안인데 왜 내가 울고 있지?

sentences.en: Some word was worse than the death of Tybalt.
sentences.ko: 티볼트의 죽음보다 더 끔찍한 말이 있었어.

sentences.en: That word murdered me.
sentences.ko: 그 말이 나를 죽였어.

sentences.en: I would like to forget it, but oh, it stays in my memory.
sentences.ko: 잊고 싶지만, 오, 그 말이 내 기억에 남아 있어.

sentences.en: It presses on me like guilty deeds press on sinners' minds.
sentences.ko: 죄지은 자의 마음을 짓누르는 죄처럼 나를 짓눌러.

sentences.en: Tybalt is dead, and Romeo is banished.
sentences.ko: 티볼트는 죽었고 로미오는 추방당했어.

sentences.en: That one word 'banished' has killed ten thousand Tybalts.
sentences.ko: '추방'이라는 그 한마디가 만 명의 티볼트를 죽였어.

sentences.en: Tybalt's death was enough sadness if it had ended there.
sentences.ko: 그게 끝이었다면 티볼트의 죽음만으로도 충분히 슬펐을 거야.

sentences.en: Perhaps sadness likes company.
sentences.ko: 슬픔이 동무를 좋아한다면 말이야.

sentences.en: Then why did the news of Tybalt's death not come with 'your father is dead,' or your mother, or both?
sentences.ko: 그렇다면 왜 티볼트의 죽음 소식이 '네 아버지가 죽었다'거나 네 어머니, 혹은 둘 다 죽었다는 말과 함께 오지 않았니?

sentences.en: I would have cried for that in the normal way.
sentences.ko: 그랬다면 보통처럼 울었을 거야.

sentences.en: But because you followed Tybalt's death with 'Romeo is banished', speaking that word means everyone is killed.
sentences.ko: 하지만 티볼트의 죽음 뒤에 '로미오는 추방당했다'는 말이 따라오니, 그 말은 모두를 죽인 거나 마찬가지야.

sentences.en: Father, mother, Tybalt, Romeo, and Juliet are all dead.
sentences.ko: 아버지, 어머니, 티볼트, 로미오, 그리고 줄리엣까지 모두 죽었어.

sentences.en: Romeo is banished.
sentences.ko: 로미오는 추방당했어.

sentences.en: There is no end or limit to the death in that word.
sentences.ko: 그 단어 속의 죽음에는 끝도 한계도 없어.

sentences.en: No words can describe that sadness.
sentences.ko: 어떤 말로도 그 슬픔을 표현할 수 없어.

sentences.en: Where are my father and my mother, Nurse?
sentences.ko: 유모, 내 아버지와 어머니는 어디에 계시니?

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Weeping and wailing over Tybalt’s corse.
Will you go to them? I will bring you thither.

sentences.en: They are crying over Tybalt's body.
sentences.ko: 티볼트의 시신 앞에서 울고 계셔.

sentences.en: Will you go to them?
sentences.ko: 그분들께 가 볼래?

sentences.en: I will bring you there.
sentences.ko: 내가 데려다줄게.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Wash they his wounds with tears. Mine shall be spent,
When theirs are dry, for Romeo’s banishment.
Take up those cords. Poor ropes, you are beguil’d,
Both you and I; for Romeo is exil’d.
He made you for a highway to my bed,
But I, a maid, die maiden-widowed.
Come cords, come Nurse, I’ll to my wedding bed,
And death, not Romeo, take my maidenhead.

sentences.en: Let them wash his wounds with tears.
sentences.ko: 그분들은 눈물로 그의 상처를 씻으라지.

sentences.en: My tears will flow for Romeo's banishment when theirs are dry.
sentences.ko: 그들의 눈물이 마르면 로미오의 추방을 위해 내 눈물이 흐를 거야.

sentences.en: Take up those ropes.
sentences.ko: 그 밧줄을 집어.

sentences.en: Poor ropes, you are tricked, both you and I, because Romeo is exiled.
sentences.ko: 가여운 밧줄들아, 너희도 나도 속은 거야. 로미오가 추방당했으니까.

sentences.en: He made you as a road to my bed.
sentences.ko: 그이는 너희를 내 침대로 오는 길로 만들었는데.

sentences.en: But I will die a virgin widow.
sentences.ko: 하지만 나는 처녀인 채 과부로 죽겠지.

sentences.en: Come ropes, come Nurse.
sentences.ko: 밧줄아 가자, 유모도 가자.

sentences.en: I will go to my wedding bed.
sentences.ko: 신방으로 가겠어.

sentences.en: And death, not Romeo, will take my virginity.
sentences.ko: 로미오가 아니라 죽음이 내 순결을 가져가겠지.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Hie to your chamber. I’ll find Romeo
To comfort you. I wot well where he is.
Hark ye, your Romeo will be here at night.
I’ll to him, he is hid at Lawrence’ cell.

sentences.en: Hurry to your room.
sentences.ko: 어서 네 방으로 가거라.

sentences.en: I will find Romeo to comfort you.
sentences.ko: 내가 로미오를 찾아와 너를 위로해 줄게.

sentences.en: I know well where he is.
sentences.ko: 그가 어디 있는지 잘 알아.

sentences.en: Listen, your Romeo will be here tonight.
sentences.ko: 들어봐, 네 로미오가 오늘 밤 여기 올 거야.

sentences.en: I will go to him.
sentences.ko: 내가 그에게 갈게.

sentences.en: He is hiding at the friar's cell.
sentences.ko: 그는 신부님의 수도실에 숨어 있어.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
O find him, give this ring to my true knight,
And bid him come to take his last farewell.

sentences.en: Please find him.
sentences.ko: 꼭 그이를 찾아 줘.

sentences.en: Give this ring to my true knight.
sentences.ko: 이 반지를 내 진정한 기사에게 전해 줘.

sentences.en: Tell him to come and say his last goodbye.
sentences.ko: 와서 마지막 작별 인사를 하라고 해 줘.

raw: Exeunt.
